title: Temporary and permanent Lahaina wildfire debris disposal sites
summary: On June 4, 2025, the committee deferred the debris item, while the County plans to begin hauling Lahaina wildfire debris to the permanent site in Central Maui on June 16, with up to 50 trucks making four trips a day. FEMA will pay tipping fees, though they may not cover all costs. The site costs just under $20 million, and the County moved $8 million in March to cover construction.

timeline.text: A council member said debris hauling will run from sunup to sundown during West Maui canoe regattas.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: A council member said permanent debris hauling in West Maui starts in June, with about 50 truck round trips a day.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: Officials said they will tell the Council when a closing date for the temporary debris site is known.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The county is working with state and federal partners on an alternate truck route for moving debris.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: Moving debris from the temporary site to the permanent site is expected to be reimbursable while the federal mission continues.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said there is no plan to mix everyday trash with the Lahaina debris.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: Officials hope to have the permanent site ready in the early-to-middle part of next year.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: Officials said losing federal help would mean the county pays for and runs the debris work itself.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said the county dropped eminent domain, a court process to take land, for a different parcel.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The parcel called unit three, where the permanent site will go, costs $2,477,550.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The county is asking for $4 million to buy two parcels for a permanent wildfire debris disposal site.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: One testifier asked why the wildfire debris site is called "permanent."
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: All wildfire debris, whether owners opted in or out of the government program, will end up at the permanent site in Central Maui.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The permanent site for Lahaina wildfire debris is the Central Maui Landfill, with a temporary site planned next to it.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The department will refine its debris site request and come back with a revised budget amendment.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The environmental management director asked to file (close out) Bill 40, a budget bill for debris disposal sites.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
